# Error codes

<!-- Generated by `rivet schema errors` from the code registry in src/error.rs. Do not edit. -->

Every failure rivet names carries a stable `RIVET_<FAMILY>_<NAME>` code: in `--json-errors` output as `code`, and as a `[CODE]` prefix on the text error line. The KIND decides the exit code.

| exit | meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | usage — fix the config or the command; retrying fails the same way |
| 2 | a transient failure, or busy (another live rivet process holds the lease or lock this command needs) — retry the same command |
| 3 | integrity — the data may be wrong; stop and investigate |
| 4 | schema drift — the source shape changed; review before re-running |
| 5 | refusal — rivet stopped on purpose to protect data; a human decides |
| 6 | internal — an invariant did not hold; a bug, please report it |

| code | kind | exit | what to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RIVET_CONFIG_NO_EXPORTS` | usage | 1 | declare at least one export under `exports:` |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CHUNK_COUNT_INVALID` | usage | 1 | set `chunk_count` to 1 or more |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CHUNK_BY_DAYS_INVALID` | usage | 1 | set `chunk_by_days` to 1 or more |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CHUNK_COLUMN_NOT_INTEGER` | usage | 1 | use `chunk_by_key:` (keyset), an integer column, or `mode: full` |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_DUPLICATE_EXPORT` | usage | 1 | give every export a unique `name` |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CDC_RESOURCE_CONFLICT` | usage | 1 | give each CDC export its own slot / server_id / checkpoint path |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CDC_ROLLOVER_INVALID` | usage | 1 | set `cdc.rollover` to 1 or more, or omit it |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CDC_CONTINUOUS_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | omit `cdc.until_current` (or `--stream`) and run the bounded drain on a schedule |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CSV_LOAD_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | use `format: parquet` for an export with a `load:` section |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_LOAD_PARTITION_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | partition by a date or time `column` + `granularity`, and drop the options the target refuses |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_SOURCE_MODE_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | use a mode this source supports (MongoDB: `full`) |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_SOURCE_URL_SCHEME_MISMATCH` | usage | 1 | make `source.type` and the URL scheme name the same engine |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_KEYSET_KEY_UUID_OVERRIDE` | usage | 1 | key the keyset on another unique column, or use `mode: full` for this table |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CURSOR_COLUMN_CASE` | usage | 1 | spell `cursor_column` exactly as the result set names the column |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_COLUMN_OVERRIDE_CASE` | usage | 1 | spell the `columns:` key exactly as the result set names the column |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_FILE_UNREADABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | check the config path and its read permission, or run `rivet init` to generate one |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_YAML_INVALID` | usage | 1 | fix the YAML syntax or the key the message names, moving it to where the message shows |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_SOURCE_CONNECTION_INVALID` | usage | 1 | give `source:` exactly one connection method (`url_env`, `url`, `url_file` or complete host/user/database fields) and one password setting |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_SECRET_UNSET` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | export the environment variable (or pass the `--param`) the message names, or make the named file readable |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_EXPORT_SOURCE_INVALID` | usage | 1 | give the export exactly one of `query`, `query_file` (a relative path inside the config directory), `table` (`<name>` or `<schema>.<name>`) or `tables` |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_MODE_SETTING_INVALID` | usage | 1 | add the setting the export's mode requires, or remove the setting the mode does not take, as the message names |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_DESTINATION_AUTH_INVALID` | usage | 1 | configure one complete auth mode for the destination (keys, a credentials file, or `allow_anonymous`) and drop the others |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT_UNSAFE` | usage | 1 | drop `endpoint:` to use the provider default, or point it at a loopback emulator with `allow_anonymous: true` |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE` | usage | 1 | set the value in the range or form the message names, and set only one of two mutually exclusive sizing knobs |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CDC_SHAPE_INVALID` | usage | 1 | list each captured table once, in a shape this source and destination take, with at most one baseline per table |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CSV_COMPRESSION_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | use `format: parquet` for compression, or set `compression: none` / `compression_profile: none` |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_TLS_VERIFICATION_DOWNGRADE` | usage | 1 | drop the danger knob and trust a private CA with `tls.ca_file`, or omit the explicit `mode:` for a loopback dev container |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_LOAD_BLOCK_INVALID` | usage | 1 | declare the warehouse in a top-level `load:` block and override only what the export and target take |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_PATH_UNSAFE` | usage | 1 | use a plain name and a bucket-relative path: no `/`, `\`, `..`, NUL, leading `.` or URI scheme |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_ROW_HASH_INVALID` | usage | 1 | list each column of one table once under `meta_columns.row_hash`, or use `row_hash: true` |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_COLUMN_OVERRIDE_TABLE_UNKNOWN` | usage | 1 | use a bare column key, or qualify it with a table this export captures |
| `RIVET_TYPE_UNSAFE_MAPPING` | usage | 1 | add a `columns:` override the engine delivers exactly, CAST or drop the column in the export's `query:`, or run without `--strict` to accept it with a warning |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | raise `tuning.statement_timeout_s`, or narrow the chunk |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CURSOR_FINER_THAN_MICROSECOND` | refusal | 5 | cursor on a column at microsecond precision or coarser, or cast the cursor to TIMESTAMP(6) in a curated query |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_FOREIGN_CHECKPOINT` | refusal | 5 | re-baseline the stream: delete the checkpoint, empty the export's destination, clear its `cdc_snapshot` rows, give it `cdc.initial: snapshot`, then re-run |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_CHECKPOINT_SHARED` | refusal | 5 | give the export a `cdc.checkpoint` of its own and keep the shared file, the other export's position; with `cdc.initial: snapshot` its first run re-reads every table |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_CHECKPOINT_INVALID` | refusal | 5 | restore the checkpoint file, or re-baseline the stream: delete it, empty the export's destination, clear its `cdc_snapshot` rows, give it `cdc.initial: snapshot`, then re-run |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_LOG_GAP` | refusal | 5 | restore the missing log, or re-baseline the stream: delete the checkpoint, empty the export's destination, clear its `cdc_snapshot` rows, give it `cdc.initial: snapshot`, then re-run |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_TRUNCATED` | refusal | 5 | re-baseline the stream: delete the checkpoint (PostgreSQL: first advance the slot past the truncate), empty the export's destination, clear its `cdc_snapshot` rows, give it `cdc.initial: snapshot`, then re-run |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_UNDECODABLE` | refusal | 5 | re-baseline the stream: delete the checkpoint, empty the export's destination, clear its `cdc_snapshot` rows, give it `cdc.initial: snapshot`, then re-run |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_CELL_UNSUPPORTED` | refusal | 5 | leave the column out of the capture (SQL Server: @captured_column_list), then re-baseline the stream: delete the checkpoint, empty the export's destination, clear its `cdc_snapshot` rows, give it `cdc.initial: snapshot`, then re-run |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_PREREQUISITE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | apply the setup statement the message names, then re-run (docs/reference/cdc.md) |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_VALUE_UNREPRESENTABLE` | refusal | 5 | map the value to a representable one in the export's `query:`, or exclude the column |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_PROBE_UNREADABLE` | refusal | 5 | chunk, page or partition the export on a column of a type the message lists, remove `parallel:` from a keyset export, or use `mode: full` |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_COLUMNS_CHANGED_UNDER_READ` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | run the export again: the next run probes and reads the table as it is now |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_OVERRIDE_WIRE_MISMATCH` | usage | 1 | remove or correct the column's `columns:` override (batch: or CAST the column to that type in the export's `query:`; CDC: then re-snapshot the table) |
| `RIVET_STATE_URL_SCHEME_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | set `RIVET_STATE_URL` to a `postgres://` or `postgresql://` URL or to `sqlite:<path>`, or unset it to keep the state in the SQLite file beside the config |
| `RIVET_STATE_URL_LEAVES_STATE_BEHIND` | refusal | 5 | copy the state beside the config to the path `RIVET_STATE_URL` names with every run stopped (`sqlite3 <old> ".backup <new>"`), or unset RIVET_STATE_URL |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_SESSION_TIME_ZONE_NOT_APPLIED` | refusal | 5 | set `default_time_zone = '+00:00'` on the MySQL server, keep rivet's session variables on one backend in the proxy (ProxySQL: session-variable tracking, no multiplexing for rivet's user), or connect directly |
| `RIVET_CLI_CHECK_REPORTED_ERRORS` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | fix what the ERROR lines above name (the source, the state, the destination), then run `rivet check` again |
| `RIVET_STATE_URL_TLS_REQUIRED` | refusal | 5 | add `?sslmode=require` (or `verify-ca` / `verify-full`) to `RIVET_STATE_URL` with TLS enabled on the state server, or `?sslmode=disable` to accept plaintext on a private network |
| `RIVET_STATE_NOT_WRITABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | make the state database writable (the SQLite file and its directory, a read-only filesystem, a read-only role) and run again; the export did not start |
| `RIVET_STATE_CURSOR_NOT_STORED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | repair the state database before the next run; the rows are delivered, and the next run delivers them again from the previous cursor |
| `RIVET_STATE_SCHEMA_NEWER` | refusal | 5 | upgrade rivet, or point this binary at a state DB it created |
| `RIVET_STATE_BACKUP_FAILED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | free disk space or make the state writable for the copy (SQLite: the directory beside the state file; PostgreSQL: CREATE on the database) and run again; the state was not migrated, and the previous rivet release still opens it |
| `RIVET_STATE_CURSOR_OWNER_MISMATCH` | refusal | 5 | `rivet state reset -c <config> --export <name>` to start the new cursor with a full pass, or restore the previous cursor column |
| `RIVET_STATE_CURSOR_INCOMPARABLE` | refusal | 5 | `rivet state reset -c <config> --export <name>` starts the cursor over with a full pass |
| `RIVET_STATE_CURSOR_PAST_MANIFEST` | refusal | 5 | `rivet state reset -c <config> --export <name>` starts the cursor over with a full pass |
| `RIVET_STATE_CURSOR_STREAM_MISMATCH` | refusal | 5 | give each export that shares this state database its own name; if this export was edited (another table, another schema, another `query:` filter), restore what it read, or `rivet state reset -c <config> --export <name>` starts what it reads now with a full pass (it discards the progress that name holds on this source), or `rivet state accept -c <config> --export <name>` keeps the stored progress and records it as belonging to what the export reads now (rows of it below that progress are not delivered) |
| `RIVET_STATE_CURSOR_DESTINATION_MISMATCH` | refusal | 5 | restore the `destination` and `format` the export had to continue from the stored progress, or `rivet state reset -c <config> --export <name>` starts over with a full pass delivered where the config points now (the parts already delivered stay where they are: empty that location first if the full pass lands in it too) |
| `RIVET_STATE_INTERRUPTED_RUN_OWNER_MISMATCH` | refusal | 5 | restore the settings the interrupted run had (its mode, its checkpoint, its format) and run once to finish it, then change them; or abandon it with the command the message names (`rivet state reset` for a keyset run, `rivet state reset-chunks` for a range-chunk run) and the next run starts with a full pass |
| `RIVET_STATE_CDC_TABLE_REJOINED` | refusal | 5 | re-baseline the table the message names: move every file out of its directory in the destination, delete its `cdc_snapshot` row from the state DB, truncate its `__changes` table if a warehouse load consumes the stream, then re-run |
| `RIVET_STATE_CHUNK_RUN_OWNER_UNKNOWN` | refusal | 5 | `rivet state reset-chunks -c <config> --export <name>` abandons the run; the next run of each config starts a fresh pass |
| `RIVET_STATE_CHUNK_RUN_SUPERSEDED` | refusal | 5 | `rivet state reset-chunks -c <config> --export <name>` abandons the run; the next run starts a fresh pass |
| `RIVET_STATE_KEYSET_SEQUENTIAL_ANCHOR_UNFINISHED` | refusal | 5 | re-run once with `parallel: 1` to finish the interrupted run, then raise `parallel:` |
| `RIVET_STATE_RUN_IN_PROGRESS` | busy | 2 | wait for the run to finish, or stop its process, then repeat the command |
| `RIVET_STATE_CHUNK_CHECKPOINT_GONE` | refusal | 5 | run the export again: it starts a new chunk run (the parts the lost run wrote stay in the destination, in no manifest) |
| `RIVET_STATE_CHUNK_PLAN_CHANGED` | refusal | 5 | restore the query and the chunk settings the interrupted run had and run once to finish it; or `rivet state reset-chunks -c <config> --export <name>` abandons it and the next run starts over |
| `RIVET_STATE_CHUNK_WINDOWS_BROKEN` | refusal | 5 | `rivet state reset-chunks -c <config> --export <name>` abandons the run; the next run plans the export again and reads every key |
| `RIVET_STATE_LEASE_KEEPER_UNAVAILABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | free a connection on the state database (rivet holds one per worker plus one for the lease keeper), raise the open-file limit, or lower `--pool`, then run again; nothing ran under the lease |
| `RIVET_STATE_LEASE_LOST` | busy | 2 | wait for the other `rivet load` or `rivet compact` of that table to end, then run again; nothing was written to the warehouse |
| `RIVET_PLAN_SOURCE_UNREADABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | fix what the message names (the connection, the credentials, or the table the export reads), then run `rivet plan` again |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_COLLECTION_NOT_FOUND` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | correct the export's `table:` (a dotted collection name is written whole), or create the collection |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_TABLE_NOT_FOUND` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | correct the export's `table:` (or the relation its `query:` reads), or remove the export from `exports:` if the table was dropped on purpose |
| `RIVET_DEST_CONTAINER_NOT_FOUND` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | create the bucket or container, or correct `destination.bucket` |
| `RIVET_DEST_RELATIVE_PATH_MOVED` | refusal | 5 | move the export's files from the directory under the working directory to the one beside the config, or make `destination.path` absolute |
| `RIVET_DEST_ALREADY_COMPLETE` | refusal | 5 | pass `--force` with `--resume` to continue an interrupted run or, with none, run as a plain run does (new parts beside the complete export); or use another destination prefix |
| `RIVET_LOAD_VALUE_OUT_OF_TARGET_RANGE` | refusal | 5 | the warehouse type cannot hold this value; declare a wider type (e.g. String) for the column, or fix the source value |
| `RIVET_LOAD_COUNT_MISMATCH` | integrity | 3 | compare the warehouse table with the run's manifest before re-running; the source is kept |
| `RIVET_LOAD_LEASE_LOST_DURING_WRITE` | integrity | 3 | compare the warehouse table with the source before relying on it: another load or compact may have written it at the same time; the next `rivet load` loads the same runs again |
| `RIVET_LOAD_ADOPTION_COLUMN_MISMATCH` | refusal | 5 | add the export's new columns to the table (`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`) and re-run; do not rename it aside |
| `RIVET_LOAD_TARGET_NOT_RIVETS` | refusal | 5 | the warehouse object exists and this state DB has no record of rivet loading it: drop or rename it, or load into another table |
| `RIVET_LOAD_IDENTIFIER_UNSAFE` | usage | 1 | rename the column or table in the source, or alias it in the export's `query:`, to a plain identifier ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) |
| `RIVET_LOAD_KEY_COLUMN_INVALID` | usage | 1 | name only columns the export delivers, in a type and number the target takes, under `pk:` / `cluster_by:` / `partition:` in the export's `load:` block (or add the column to the export's SELECT), as the message names |
| `RIVET_LOAD_PRIMARY_KEY_MISSING` | usage | 1 | declare the key under the export's `load:` block, e.g. `pk: [id]` |
| `RIVET_LOAD_RESERVED_COLUMN` | usage | 1 | rename or exclude the column in the export's query, or load the table with `mode: full` |
| `RIVET_LOAD_LOOKALIKE_COLUMN` | usage | 1 | rename the column with Cyrillic look-alike letters in the source to Latin letters, as the message names |
| `RIVET_LOAD_TARGET_COLLISION` | usage | 1 | give each export its own `table:` or destination |
| `RIVET_LOAD_STAGING_PREFIX_INVALID` | usage | 1 | set a non-empty `destination.prefix` with no `{date}` or `{run_id}` above `{partition}`, and a literal segment before `{partition}` |
| `RIVET_LOAD_DESTINATION_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | stage the export to a destination the target reads (GCS; ClickHouse also S3 and Azure), or drop the `load:` block |
| `RIVET_LOAD_PARTITION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` | usage | 1 | partition by a coarser `granularity`, or export a narrower range per run, as the message names |
| `RIVET_LOAD_FILE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | usage | 1 | load after fewer runs, or write fewer, larger parts (lower the export's parallelism) |
| `RIVET_LOAD_COLUMN_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | CAST or drop the column in the export's `query:`, or add a `columns:` override to a type the target takes |
| `RIVET_LOAD_TLS_CA_INVALID` | usage | 1 | point `load.ca_file` at a PEM bundle holding the server's CA certificate |
| `RIVET_LOAD_EMPTY_RUN_UNSUPPORTED` | refusal | 5 | TRUNCATE the warehouse table by hand, or keep its previous rows knowingly; nothing was written |
| `RIVET_LOAD_RUN_NOT_LOADABLE` | refusal | 5 | re-run the export so a complete run (a Success manifest and every part it declares) is under the prefix the load reads, then load |
| `RIVET_LOAD_STAGING_OBJECT_UNSAFE` | refusal | 5 | investigate the staging bucket: remove the object the message names, then re-run the export and the load |
| `RIVET_LOAD_SOURCES_SHARED` | refusal | 5 | give each export and each source its own destination prefix and its own target table |
| `RIVET_LOAD_COLUMN_RESPELLED` | refusal | 5 | load the older runs by hand under the old spelling as the message describes, then delete their manifests; every run stays staged |
| `RIVET_LOAD_TARGET_OBJECT_CONFLICT` | refusal | 5 | drop or rename the warehouse object the message names, or align the config with it; nothing was written |
| `RIVET_LOAD_COMPACT_BASE_MISSING` | refusal | 5 | load the backfill first (the `cdc.backfill:` export builds the base), or drop the buffer to discard its changes |
| `RIVET_LOAD_CHANGELOG_PARTITION_CHANGED` | refusal | 5 | keep the change log's partitioning in the config, or rebuild it as the message names (`rivet load --rebuild-changelog`, or by hand where policies must be kept) |
| `RIVET_LOAD_BUFFER_NOT_COMPACTED` | refusal | 5 | run `rivet compact` first if the buffer belongs to the current base, or drop the buffer, then re-run the load |
| `RIVET_LOAD_REBASELINE_OVER_CHANGES` | refusal | 5 | TRUNCATE the change log the message names, then re-run the same `rivet load` |
| `RIVET_LOAD_TABLE_BUSY` | busy | 2 | wait for the other `rivet load` or `rivet compact` of that table to end, then run again |
| `RIVET_LOAD_MANIFEST_INCONSISTENT` | integrity | 3 | investigate the run's manifest and parts before loading; re-run the export to replace them |
| `RIVET_LOAD_SOURCE_FILE_MISMATCH` | integrity | 3 | investigate the extract before loading; to accept the drift, set `allow_source_drift: true` in the export's `load:` block |
| `RIVET_LOAD_COPY_COUNT_MISMATCH` | integrity | 3 | compare the tables the message names before re-running; rivet left them for inspection |
| `RIVET_LOAD_LEDGER_UNREADABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | restore the state backend (lower `--pool` if workers could not reconnect), then re-run |
| `RIVET_LOAD_RUN_LANDED_DURING_LOAD` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | run `rivet load` again: it types from the newest run |
| `RIVET_LOAD_WAREHOUSE_AUTH_FAILED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | renew the warehouse credentials (`gcloud auth application-default login`, a service-account key, or the target's connection settings) |
| `RIVET_LOAD_WAREHOUSE_ACCESS_DENIED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | grant the load's identity the warehouse permission the message names |
| `RIVET_LOAD_WAREHOUSE_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | create the dataset or database the load writes into, or correct the names of the `load:` target |
| `RIVET_LOAD_WAREHOUSE_REJECTED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | read the warehouse's reason in the message and fix what it names, then re-run |
| `RIVET_LOAD_WAREHOUSE_UNAVAILABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | re-run the load later; the warehouse answered with a transient failure on every retry |
| `RIVET_LOAD_WAREHOUSE_ANSWER_UNREADABLE` | internal | 6 | the warehouse answered in a shape rivet does not read — report it with the message |
| `RIVET_INTERNAL_LOAD_INVARIANT` | internal | 6 | a load invariant did not hold — a bug; report it with the message |
| `RIVET_VALIDATE_FAILED` | integrity | 3 | run `rivet validate` on the prefix and settle each failed part before loading it; the export itself completed |
| `RIVET_VALIDATE_UNVERIFIED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | restore read access to the destination and run `rivet validate`; the export itself completed |
| `RIVET_INTERNAL_VALUE_CONVERTER` | internal | 6 | a value changed between the source and the written part — a bug; report it with the column's type |
| `RIVET_INTERNAL_SPILL` | internal | 6 | the CDC spill log is inconsistent — a bug or a damaged spill directory; report it and re-run |
| `RIVET_INTERNAL_TYPE_BUILDER` | internal | 6 | a column builder got a type it cannot build — a bug; report it with the column's type |
| `RIVET_LOAD_SPEC_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED` | usage | 1 | set the source's variable (`url_env:` / `password_env:`) for `rivet load` as for `rivet run` |
| `RIVET_CLI_EXPORT_UNKNOWN` | usage | 1 | pass `--export` a name declared under `exports:` in this config |
| `RIVET_CLI_TABLE_UNKNOWN` | usage | 1 | pass `--table` a warehouse table this config loads, as the message lists |
| `RIVET_CLI_RUN_ID_EXPORT_MISMATCH` | usage | 1 | pass the `--export` the run id belongs to, or omit `--run-id` |
| `RIVET_CLI_OPTION_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | drop the option, or give the command the config, export or mode it takes, as the message names |
| `RIVET_CLI_REPORT_INVALID` | usage | 1 | pass the report `rivet reconcile --report` wrote for this export |
| `RIVET_CLI_OUTPUT_UNWRITABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | check the output path and its directory's write permission |
| `RIVET_CLI_INPUT_UNREADABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | check the path passed to the command and its read permission |
| `RIVET_CLI_EXECUTABLE_UNRESOLVED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | run rivet from a binary the OS can resolve: not deleted, unmounted or replaced while it runs |
| `RIVET_CLI_TEST_FAULT_INJECTED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | unset `RIVET_TEST_ERROR_AT`; the fault is rivet's own test hook, not the source |
| `RIVET_PLAN_NOTHING_TO_PLAN` | usage | 1 | run the CDC streams and backfill recipes with `rivet run`; `rivet plan` plans batch exports only |
| `RIVET_PLAN_ARTIFACT_STALE` | refusal | 5 | regenerate the plan with `rivet plan`, or pass `--force` to apply it as it is |
| `RIVET_PLAN_ARTIFACT_NO_CREDENTIALS` | usage | 1 | re-plan from a config that gives the source `url_env:` or `url_file:` |
| `RIVET_PLAN_PARTITION_TOKEN_UNEXPANDED` | usage | 1 | run the config (`rivet apply <config.yaml>` or `rivet run`), or drop `{partition}` from the destination |
| `RIVET_PLAN_REJECTED` | usage | 1 | fix the config so the rule the message names passes; `rivet check` reports the same rules |
| `RIVET_PLAN_CHUNK_KEY_SPARSE` | usage | 1 | set an explicit `chunk_count:` (or a larger `chunk_size:`), page by `chunk_by_key:`, or use `mode: full` |
| `RIVET_PLAN_CHUNK_KEY_NULL` | refusal | 5 | chunk on a NOT NULL column, drop the NULL rows with `WHERE <column> IS NOT NULL` in the query, or use `mode: full` |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_SETTLE_COLUMN_NOT_TEMPORAL` | usage | 1 | point `settle.column` at a date or timestamp column, or omit it to settle on the cursor |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_SPLIT_PREFIX_UNSTABLE` | usage | 1 | give the split export a destination without run-varying placeholders (`{export}` and `{table}` are stable) |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_EXPORT_NAME_RESERVED` | usage | 1 | rename the export: `<name>#<n>` names are reserved for split units |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_BATCH_MEMORY_EXCEEDED` | usage | 1 | lower `batch_size`, or set `on_batch_memory_exceeded: auto_shrink` |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CDC_CAPTURE_INSTANCE_MISMATCH` | usage | 1 | set `table:` to the relation the capture instance emits, or point `capture_instance:` at the table you meant |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_VALUE_TOO_LARGE` | usage | 1 | raise `tuning.max_value_mb`, or set it to 0 to disable the guard |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_KEYSET_KEY_COARSE` | refusal | 5 | page on a unique key rivet reads exactly: an integer, text, uuid or date column, or a timestamp at microsecond precision or coarser (cast it in a curated query) |
| `RIVET_STATE_CHUNK_RUN_MISSING` | usage | 1 | set `chunk_checkpoint: true` and run the export before `rivet reconcile` |
| `RIVET_STATE_CHUNK_RUN_UNFINISHED` | refusal | 5 | `rivet run … --resume` continues the unfinished chunk run; `rivet state reset-chunks` abandons it |
| `RIVET_DEST_MANIFEST_MISSING` | usage | 1 | finish the export (a complete run writes `manifest.json` at the prefix) before `rivet repair` |
| `RIVET_DEST_MANIFEST_NOT_WRITTEN` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | restore write access to the destination prefix and run again; until a run completes, no manifest names the parts already there |
| `RIVET_DEST_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | run again: the object vanished between rivet's two reads of it; if it repeats, check what else writes to the prefix |
| `RIVET_DEST_UPLOAD_CORRUPTED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | run again: the part is uploaded afresh; if it repeats, check the network path and any proxy in front of the destination |
| `RIVET_DEST_PREFIX_UNLISTABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | restore list access to the destination prefix and retry the resume |
| `RIVET_DEST_COMMITTED_PART_GONE` | refusal | 5 | `rivet state reset -c <config> --export <name>` (keyset) or `rivet state reset-chunks` (range chunks) so the range is re-read, or export into a fresh prefix |
| `RIVET_DEST_CONTROL_ARTIFACT_INVALID` | refusal | 5 | inspect the manifest at the prefix: one rivet wrote parses and is small; restore or remove it, then run again |
| `RIVET_DEST_PART_ROWS_MISMATCH` | integrity | 3 | stop and report it: a writer bug or a damaged disk; the part was not committed |
| `RIVET_RUN_UNITS_FAILED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | fix the first cause the message names and run again; a checkpointed run resumes from where it stopped |
| `RIVET_RUN_RECONCILE_UNVERIFIED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | run again to obtain the reconcile assurance, or drop `--reconcile`; the export completed |
| `RIVET_INTERNAL_RUN_INVARIANT` | internal | 6 | a run invariant did not hold — a bug; report it with the message |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_SOURCE_URL_INVALID` | usage | 1 | write the source URL in the form the message shows (`<scheme>://user:password@host:port/<database or service>`) |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_SOURCE_OPTION_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | remove the setting the message names: this source type does not support it |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_SOURCE_FEATURE_MISSING` | usage | 1 | run a rivet built with the feature the message names (the release binaries include it) |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_TABLE_UNRESOLVED` | usage | 1 | set `table:` to the one base table the capture follows, qualified `schema.table` as the catalog spells it, as the message explains |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_TABLE_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | export the table in batch (`mode: full`), or capture a table the message's supported list covers |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_TRANSACTION_TOO_LARGE` | usage | 1 | split the source transaction, or raise RIVET_CDC_MAX_TX_ROWS / RIVET_CDC_MAX_TX_BYTES when a transaction this large is expected |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_QUERY_COLUMN_UNREFERENCEABLE` | usage | 1 | give the column an alias in the export's `query:` (e.g. `... AS row_id`) |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | the process could not start the async runtime its driver needs (out of file descriptors or threads): raise the open-files limit (`ulimit -n`) or lower parallelism, then rerun |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CONNECT_FAILED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | check the host, port, credentials and TLS settings in the source URL; the driver's own words follow the colon |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_QUERY_FAILED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | fix what the server's words name (the statement, the login's rights on the object, or the session), then run again |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_SPILL_UNLOCKABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | point RIVET_CDC_SPILL_DIR at a local, flock-capable filesystem, or raise the rollover memory cap so the transaction stays in memory |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_CDC_SPILL_UNWRITABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | free space on the spill directory's filesystem (RIVET_CDC_SPILL_DIR, else beside the checkpoint) and check its write permission, then re-run |
| `RIVET_INTERNAL_SOURCE_INVARIANT` | internal | 6 | a source reader invariant did not hold — a bug; report it with the message |
| `RIVET_SOURCE_KEYSET_KEY_UNORDERED` | refusal | 5 | remove `page_size`, `resume` and `parallel` so the collection is read in one ordered scan, or fix the `_id` values the message names |
| `RIVET_CLI_VALUE_INVALID` | usage | 1 | pass the option a value in the form the message names |
| `RIVET_CLI_RUN_ID_UNKNOWN` | usage | 1 | pass a run id `rivet state runs -c <config>` lists |
| `RIVET_CLI_PREFLIGHT_FAILED` | usage | 1 | fix each check the output above names, then run the command again |
| `RIVET_CLI_PREFLIGHT_UNVERIFIED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | run `rivet doctor` again once the source or destination the output names answers |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_TARGET_UNKNOWN` | usage | 1 | set `target:` (or `--target`) to one of the names the message lists |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_TLS_CA_INVALID` | usage | 1 | point `tls.ca_file` at a readable PEM file holding the CA certificate |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_FORMAT_COLUMN_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | change `format:`, or cast or drop the column in the export's query |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_META_COLUMN_COLLISION` | usage | 1 | alias the source column in a `query:`, or turn the colliding meta column off |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_CANON_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED` | usage | 1 | leave the column out of the gate the message names, or cast it in the query |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_QUALITY_COLUMN_UNKNOWN` | usage | 1 | name columns the export projects under `quality:`, or add them to the query |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_COLUMN_OVERRIDE_TYPE_INVALID` | usage | 1 | give the `columns:` override one of the type names the message lists, with `decimal(precision,scale)` in range |
| `RIVET_CONFIG_DESTINATION_SETTING_MISSING` | usage | 1 | set the destination key the message names |
| `RIVET_DEST_CREDENTIALS_INVALID` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | issue the destination a fresh, complete credential (a new SAS, service-account key or `gcloud auth application-default login`) |
| `RIVET_DEST_PREFIX_MODE_MISMATCH` | refusal | 5 | give the export its own destination prefix; a batch and a CDC export must not share one |
| `RIVET_DEST_IO_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | raise the process's thread and open-file limits, or lower the export parallelism, then run again |
| `RIVET_INIT_CDC_NAME_TAKEN` | refusal | 5 | write the config under another `-o` name: the stem names its checkpoint and destination |
| `RIVET_INIT_CONFIG_EXISTS` | refusal | 5 | move the existing config aside, or write elsewhere with `-o <new-path>` |
| `RIVET_INIT_TABLE_NOT_FOUND` | usage | 1 | correct `--table` (and `--schema`), or grant the user SELECT on the table |
| `RIVET_INIT_NO_TABLES` | usage | 1 | point `--schema` at a schema the user can read, and loosen `--include` / `--exclude` |
| `RIVET_LOAD_SPLIT_GENERATIONS_MIXED` | refusal | 5 | load from a fresh destination prefix, or clear the stale split generation, and run again |
| `RIVET_LOAD_SPEC_MISSING` | refusal | 5 | run `rivet run` for the export the message names so its column types are recorded, then load again |
| `RIVET_MCP_REQUEST_INVALID` | usage | 1 | send a method and tool name `tools/list` advertises, with `params` |
| `RIVET_PLAN_ARTIFACT_INVALID` | usage | 1 | pass a plan file `rivet plan` wrote, unedited; run `rivet plan` again to regenerate it |
| `RIVET_PLAN_CHUNK_KEY_UNUSABLE` | usage | 1 | set `chunk_column:` (integer) or `chunk_by_key:` (a single-column NOT NULL unique key of a supported type), add such an index, or use `mode: full` |
| `RIVET_STATE_BACKEND_FAILED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | check the state database (the SQLite file, or the `RIVET_STATE_URL` server and the role's rights), then run again |
| `RIVET_STATE_FILE_CORRUPT` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | move the state file aside (rivet rebuilds it; cursors and skip-ledgers start fresh), or restore it from a backup |
| `RIVET_STATE_COPY_SOURCE_EMPTY` | usage | 1 | name the config whose `.rivet_state.db` holds the state, or its `RIVET_STATE_URL=sqlite:<path>` |
| `RIVET_STATE_COPY_TARGET_MISSING` | usage | 1 | pass `--to postgresql://…`, or set RIVET_STATE_URL to the PostgreSQL state |
| `RIVET_STATE_COPY_TARGET_NOT_EMPTY` | refusal | 5 | copy into a PostgreSQL database (or schema) that holds no rivet state |
| `RIVET_STATE_COPY_COUNT_MISMATCH` | integrity | 3 | nothing was committed; keep using the SQLite state and report the table the message names |
| `RIVET_STATE_MIGRATION_LOCKED` | environment | 2 if transient, else 1 | wait for the other rivet process migrating this state database to finish, then run again |
| `RIVET_INTERNAL_DEST_INVARIANT` | internal | 6 | a destination invariant did not hold — a bug; report it with the message |
| `RIVET_INTERNAL_STATE_INVARIANT` | internal | 6 | a state-store invariant did not hold — a bug; report it with the message |
